validity.researcher_notes: Marysville Connector Pipeline is a real, certificated LDC (local distribution company) supply expansion by Columbia Gas of Ohio. It is correctly classified as transmission (an interstate transmission line delivering to a local utility). Status is correctly recorded as shelved: the project was approved by Ohio OPSB in August 2020, granted a 3-year extension in June 2023, but has had no construction updates since 2023 due to ongoing land-rights litigation over a Bailey family agricultural easement. It remains shelved, not cancelled - the easement issue is ongoing and permits remain valid. Project exists and is real.

validity.researcher_notes:
RE-RESEARCHED 2026-09-14 by the orchestrator. The prior pass left this unit UNRESOLVED with the note 'Did not access those sources' -- that is not an UNRESOLVED, which means nothing was FOUND, never that something was not LOOKED FOR. The sources it named were checked and they answer the question.

OWNER = Columbia Gas of Ohio, Inc. (100%), a NiSource local distribution company. NiSource Inc.'s own SEC-filed Exhibit 21, 'SUBSIDIARIES OF NISOURCE INC. as of December 31, 2025', lists under COLUMBIA OPERATIONS: 'Columbia Gas of Ohio, Inc. | Ohio'. The same exhibit contains NO entry for Columbia Gas Transmission -- as expected, because NiSource sold its interstate transmission business (Columbia Pipeline Group, which holds Columbia Gas Transmission LLC) to TransCanada/TC Energy in 2016 and retained the state LDCs. EIA independently names the operator 'Columbia Gas of Ohio' for this project in every release that carries it (Aug 2026 release, 'Natural Gas Pipeline Projects' sheet, Excel row 76; also 2021-01 row 74, 2025-07 row 64, 2026-01 row 73, 2026-05 row 75) -- but EIA supports OPERATOR only; it has no ownership column at all, so the equity fact rests on the Exhibit 21.

WHY THE SHEET'S 'Columbia Gas Transmission' IS WRONG, AND THE TRAP THAT MAKES IT LOOK RIGHT: EIA's 2025-07 release records this project's docket as 'FERC Blanket Certificate Notification (under CP82-479-000'. CP82-479 is TC Energy's blanket certificate, not Columbia Gas of Ohio's -- the very next row of that same EIA sheet (row 65) reads 'Maysville Expansion Project | TC Energy | FERC Blanket Certificate (Docket No. CP82-479-000) for main-line tie-in'. So the interstate company appears here as the TIE-IN COUNTERPARTY whose mainline this 2.18-mile Ohio-to-Ohio LDC connector ties into, under whose blanket authority the notification was filed. That is a connection, not ownership. Same correction, same reasoning, and the same Exhibit 21 as the sibling row P4447 (Northern Loop Project, also Columbia Gas of Ohio, also Ohio-to-Ohio, also carried on the sheet under PipelineName 'Columbia Gas Transmission').

CAVEAT ON THE REF: the Exhibit 21 establishes corporate parentage and does NOT name this pipeline, so name_found is false and the tier is medium, not high. The second source (EIA) is an operator source, deliberately not staged for Owner. DO NOT propagate this correction to P4446 (Virginia Electrification Project): that one is a FERC-certificated INTERSTATE project (CP21-498, Virginia), where Columbia Gas Transmission LLC genuinely is the asset entity. The discriminator is jurisdiction -- Ohio Power Siting Board / intrastate / blanket-certificate tie-in means the LDC Columbia Gas of Ohio; a FERC certificate docket means the interstate Columbia Gas Transmission LLC.
